newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-STAR QB MANNING NOT ENTERING DRAFT, WILL REMAIN AT TENNESSEE.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-STAR QB MANNING NOT ENTERING DRAFT, WILL REMAIN AT TENNESSEE.

text.p: Peyton Manning, star quarterback for the University of Tennessee, announced Wednesday he was not entering next month's NFL Draft and instead would return for a fourth season of college football.
"I am staying at Tennessee," Manning told a news conference on the school's campus, touching off a wild celebration from those attending at the Thompson-Boling Arena.

Manning, son of former NFL quarterback Archie Manning, would have been one of the top players selected had he elected to join the pros, and may have been tabbed first overall -- a pick held by the New York Jets.
Conflicting reports said that Manning would forgo his final season of eligibility or stay in school, "But that rascal really knows how to keep a secret," said Tennessee football coach Phillip Fulmer.

Manning completed 63.9 percent of his passes last season (243-of-380) for 3,287 yards and 20 touchdowns, leading Tennessee to a 10-2 record, including a victory over Northwestern in the Florida Citrus Bowl.
Manning's passing efficiency rating was seventh in the country. He also was eighth in the nation in total offence per game with an average of 286.9 yards.
